claim: The built WiFi PCIe1 stack can enumerate the BCM4389 endpoint without enabling its driver or DMA, then release host/PHY power cleanly.
oracle: Oriole initramfs pause and modules enabled; fresh backups match; watchdog feeder owns watchdog0 and host serial capture is live; endpoint vendor14e4 device4441 appears with no driver and PCI_COMMAND_MASTER clear; host/PHY unload and WLAN regulator disabled; no UFS fault; reboot removes temporary DT.

validation.user_journey: Phone temporarily leaves the desktop for diagnostics; a failed enumeration is reported, not presented as working WiFi. Preserve stock A and rootfs. Recover the known Linux graphics/touch stack after the trial.
code_reasoning: Installed boot/vendor_boot/dtbo prefixes match verified touch-stage images
No hardware autoload in paused initramfs; disable kernel module helper
Only WiFi PCI domain1; no CPIF/modem, firmware load, IOMMU or S2MPU write
Power cleanup follows IRQ and DWC cleanup; overlay remains until reboot
validation.unit: Supply, PMU, IRQ lifetime and MSI tests pass; framing decoder rejects corrupted backup transport.
validation.end_to_end: Current kernel build -> hashed USB serial staging -> paused initramfs -> guarded module load -> PCI metadata -> cleanup -> independent fresh serial read. Fault/hang recovery uses previously tested hardware watchdog.

evidence: Seven fresh off-device backups verified on host and reread on phone
boot_b/vendor_boot_b/dtbo_b prefixes match known paused initramfs images
All three candidate modules staged with manifest hashes
limitations: No WiFi association, DHCP, DNS, HTTPS or cellular acceptance from this test
No full cold-boot GPU or camera acceptance
No live removal of overlay DT; reboot required
exit_gate: Only a clean powered enumeration and cleanup permits the next DMA review. Any mismatch, UFS error, driver bind, unexpected bus-master bit or cleanup failure stops the trial and retains watchdog recovery.
